title: Medical Education: Developing Medical Cannabis Competencies. A Consensus Statement. The AMA Is Playing Catch Up
description: First, as someone who has been very critical of the medical establishment in general, and the American Medical Association in particular, I want to...
content_html_sanitized:
First, as someone who has been very critical of the medical establishment in general, and the American Medical Association in particular, I want to begin by saluting the team behind this candid “Statement.”

 

They have described how the medical establishment can catch up with the state of the art in the therapeutic use of cannabis.

 

As they say at the beginning, “The use of medical cannabis continues to expand rapidly across the US, yet most health care practitioners and trainees report feeling unprepared to counsel patients or integrate cannabis into care. Despite its clinical relevance, standardized education on medical cannabis remains absent from most medical school curricula.”

 

But, of course, I also have to say, “Better late than never.”

 

Shortly after I became National Director of NORML in 1992, we began putting a catchy slogan on our letterheads, “Stop Arresting Sick People.”

 

Well, maybe it wasn’t too “catchy”, because people wouldn’t believe that it was really happening. We had people on crutches and in wheelchairs picketing the White House and speaking at the National Press Club, but no one reported it.

 

So it went, while I was in Washington. It wasn’t until Denis Peron got Proposition 215 passed in November of 2016, that Prohibitionists had to take medical marijuana seriously. And then they got really dangerous, as my friends would find out.

 

General Barry McCaffrey, the then Drug Czar was panicked by the passing of 215, and authorized spending $1,000,000 from his huge budget to have the Institute of Medicine do a study for propaganda purposes.

See

ONDCP To Fund Review Of Scientific Evidence On Medical Marijuana. NORML Expects Institute Of Medicine To Reaffirm Marijuana’s Therapeutic Value

 

In the Spring of 1997 Peter McWilliams asked me to go to the initial public hearings at the IOM campus at Bethesda, Maryland. It was really a waste of time, but I am glad I went. It was another installment of “Yep, it really happened.”

 

The large auditorium was mostly empty. I remember one young man in a wheelchair who explained that he had MS, and then said to the panel of doctors, “I’m already in a wheelchair. Why do you want to put me in jail.”

 

Of course the doctors were horrified at the idea, and assured him that they were there for the science. I doubt if they ever saw him again. Weed was easy to get in greater Washington, so he was okay,  as long as he didn’t get busted.

 

Next there was a presentation on a study that they had done on glaucoma….To prove that marijuana didn’t work. The Feds had been forced by Bob Randall’s suit to provide glaucoma patients with medical marijuana, so this was of special interest to the Drug Czar.

See There Are None So Blind As Ophthalmologists Who Don’t Want to See: Marijuana, Glaucoma, Science And Journalism -- Analysis -- And 3 News Articles

 

The doctor explained that they had given the subjects marijuana, and it did lower intraocular pressure, but that it quickly stopped working, so it would not be a good treatment for glaucoma.

 

The auditorium was mostly empty and I was sitting in the middle (wearing a coat and tie, of course, the traditional costume of my people), so I decided to get up and ask the obvious question, “Did the subjects have glaucoma or were they healthy?”

 

“Oh, they were healthy. It wouldn’t be ethical to experiment on patients.”

 

“Understandable. But how do we know that the effect on patients would wear off?” Uh…

 

Turns out that I was sitting in the area for doctors. I had to move.

 

However, ultimately the IOM report did not say what the Czar wanted, so he did what he always did. He lied about it.

See

IOM Findings Strengthen Administrative Challenge To Repeal Marijuana’s Prohibitive Status

 

Unfortunately, while McWilliams lived long enough to see the publication of the Report, it did not even mitigate his suffering.

See

The Murder of Peter McWilliams -- An Indictment, Not an Obituary by Richard Cowan

And the AMA is just now catching up.

See

AMA Rejects Institute of Medicine, Others Support for “Compassionate Access” to Medical Marijuana

 

The AMA has come a long way over a long period of time, but in the real world where the patients have been stuck for the past thirty five plus years it has gone by very slowly.
